reason: Curative/therapeutic claim wording maps to a drug intent under Drugs & Cosmetics Act 1940 (ASU rules).
Solvent/hydroalcoholic extraction combined with therapeutic purpose suggests a concentrated medicinal product rather than food.
Daily-dietary purpose + structure-function claims + classical aqueous preparation aligns with the Ayurveda Aahara food frame.
source: FSSAI Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022

reason: Wellness-only claims in food-type dosage forms fit the Aahara category.

Classical dosage forms (Vati, Kwatha, Churna, Taila, Asava-Arishtha) with medicinal intent default to the ASU drug frame; the same form carrying only wellness claims moves to the Aahara/nutraceutical pathway.
Capsule/tablet form carrying a health claim points to a proprietary Ayurvedic medicine product licence path.
source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act (Schedule Z proprietary Ayurveda medicines)

reason: Encapsulated wellness product without curative claims fits the FSSAI Health Supplements / Nutraceuticals frame.
source: FSSAI (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use...) Regulations, 2022

reason: Topical form with skin/hair care connotation maps to the Cosmetics Rules pathway.
Curative claims without a disclaimer signal an unregistered drug intent that must move to e-AUSHADHI licensing.

A formulation that reproduces a classical First Schedule text reference with known ingredients and medicinal use is a Classical Ayurvedic medicine — it is grandfathered as a scheduled medicine and does not need a full New Drug approval.
source: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 — Rule 2(ea) & First Schedule; AYUSH CCReM

reason: A classical base carrying only dietary/wellness purpose is a food under the Ayurveda Aahara frame, not a drug.
An ingredient NOT referenced in the First Schedule with therapeutic purpose makes the formulation a New Drug, including Ayurveda-based medicines under the Section 3(p) legal fiction.
source: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 — Rule 2(ea) new drug definition; Section 3(p) D&C Act 1940

reason: A novel ingredient carrying only daily-diet/wellness framing falls to the FSSAI Ayurveda Aahara/food pathway rather than the drug frame.
Known botanical material processed through a non-traditional (solvent/supercritical/enzyme) route with medicinal intent aligns with the Phytopharmaceutical New Drug frame.
source: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 — Rule 2(ea) Phytopharmaceutical; CDSCO guidance on phytopharmaceuticals

reason: Standardised/titrated botanical extracts with quantified actives and medical claims map to the Phytopharmaceutical New Drug route.
source: CDSCO Phytopharmaceutical guidance; Rule 2(ea) D&C Rules 1945

reason: A novel/innovative manufacturing process applied to known Ayurvedic ingredients with therapeutic purpose keeps the product in the proprietary Ayurveda medicine (Schedule Z) frame requiring evidence of efficacy.
source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act (Schedule Z proprietary Ayurveda medicines); e-AUSHADHI

reason: Even a classical base becomes a proprietary medicine when the manufacturing process is materially altered from the classical method.
source: CDSCO ASU classification; e-AUSHADHI proprietary licences
